summary: Automatic host fencing slice 4a: hardware watchdog detection and reporting, the Host fencing pool setting, and the watchdog method in the fencing readiness shape — without the cluster that would arm a watchdog and without the watchdog proof kind, which are slice 4b. Each host reads /sys/class/watchdog only and NEVER opens /dev/watchdog, because on most drivers opening the device arms the timer and a host that has not been told to arm one must not be reset by having been looked at; the device is named by its sysfs name and no string literal in the detection source names a device node, which a test asserts. Classification is by kernel driver in one list (iTCO_wdt, sp5100_tco, ipmi_watchdog, hpwdt, wdat_wdt, i6300esb, mei_wdt, sbsa_gwdt are hardware; softdog is software; anything else is unknown), only hardware ever counts, and softdog is reported precisely so an operator sees why their host is not protected. The capability travels on the existing advertise peer route beside system_uuid and bmc, is recorded in the calling member's own row, is written only when the finding changes and carries no timestamp, because nothing decides anything from how long ago a host last said it. The pool gains a durable, replicated, master-owned Host fencing setting recorded as PoolMembership.host_fencing_disabled so that an absent field is on — it defaults to on, a pool recorded before it existed keeps the default, and a Controller relays it and stores nothing. Turning it on arms nothing by itself: the master reports its own prerequisite checklist (hosts, hardware watchdogs, confirmed fence devices, quorum) with its membership so an operator meets it whether or not they open the setting, and quorum is honestly unknown until 4b provides it. Every host's readiness gains a second method, kind watchdog, which in this slice can never be ready — so N-of-M is unchanged by 4a — with its own states including not_applicable at two hosts, which is not a wait and not something an operator can fix. The UI shows the watchdog line in the Fencing column and the Host fencing switch with Core's checklist and the partition-reboot consequence beside it rather than behind it. This change also closes slice 3's four verified-open review findings: a fence credential is now PARSED and never executed, so a compromised master can no longer get a root shell on every member every five minutes through a sealed replica; the profile stamp covers the credential, so rotating only a password drops the checks taken with the previous one; the stale safety comment naming the deleted fenceTargetPower is corrected; an unstamped check from an older Core degrades to dropped rather than failing the whole pass with 400, and the contract says so; and the pool fence summary moved from the pool master's row to PoolMembership.fence_summary, projected once for the pool. API impact: changed contract, implemented both sides.

guide.reason: Operators gain a new pool setting and a new line on every host row, so docs/guide/pool-authority-and-recovery.md gains 'Host fencing, and the watchdog line': what a watchdog is and why it is the only way to shut out a host that is hung rather than unreachable; that NOTHING IS ARMED in this release and the Fencing column never counts a watchdog as protection; a table of every watchdog line a row can show (hardware present but not armed, software only and why a hung kernel cannot run it, an unrecognised driver, no device, not applicable below three hosts, the setting turned off, and a host too old to report) with what to do about each; the Host fencing switch, that it is on for every pool unless turned off and that on arms nothing by itself; Core's four prerequisite lines and that quorum reads 'no quorum service yet' in this release; the partition-reboot consequence in full — an armed host that loses quorum resets itself and its running virtual machines stop, and a switch failure that splits a pool reboots the minority side — with why it is written beside a switch that is on by default; that turning the setting off needs no confirmation and changes nothing already running; and that the setting is the master's, replicated to every member and read back by a rebuilt Controller. The page's status paragraph and 'what exists today' list name it. docs/guide/README.md needs no change: the page is already listed and its title is unchanged.

api.reason: New client route POST /api/v1/pools/{id}/host-fencing (PoolHostFencingRequest{request_id, enabled}, administrator session, same origin, X-CSRF-Token): relayed to the pool master as one durable pool-host-fencing command whose PoolCommand action is host-fencing and which names no member, because the setting is the pool's. 400 for a missing pool or request_id, 401/403 for session and CSRF, 404 for an unknown pool, 409 for a replay under another payload, a master that is not fresh, or a master without pool-host-fencing-v1 (named in the message), 500 for Controller storage with nothing queued and the same request_id safe to retry. An exact replay answers 200 with the original operation and makes no second command. Core refuses it on a host that is not the master and while the pool authority is frozen or handed over, and treats it as a desired state so re-sending the recorded state succeeds. New capability protocol.PoolHostFencingCapability = pool-host-fencing-v1, advertised by Core and required by the Controller before the switch is offered at all. PoolMembership gains host_fencing_disabled (durable, replicated, master-written; the negative so an absent field is on) and fence_summary (a memory-only overlay on the reported copy). PoolMember gains watchdog (PoolHostWatchdog{kind, device, driver, identity, timeout_seconds, nowayout, in_use, devices}), reported on the existing peer route POST /api/v1/pool/advertise beside system_uuid and bmc — recorded in the calling member's own row only, refused with 400 for a kind outside the closed set or an over-length string, written only when the finding changes and carrying no timestamp. PoolFenceSummary gains host_fencing and prerequisites ([PoolFencePrerequisite{name, state, detail}], name closed to hosts/watchdogs/bmc/quorum and state to met/unmet/unknown) and MOVED from PoolFenceReadiness.pool on the master's row to PoolMembership.fence_summary, reported once for the pool; PoolFenceReadiness.pool is deleted. PoolFenceMethod.state gains not_applicable. The Controller's members projection gains host_fencing_supported and fence, and poolMemberFence gains watchdog; it relays and displays only and stores nothing. Version compatibility: a Core without the capability reports no summary and no watchdog, which the Controller shows as 'not reported' and never as ready, and the switch is not offered; a member too old to report a watchdog leaves the field absent, which never counts. Also fixed here, from slice 3's independent review: PoolFenceCheck.profile is now optional on the wire, so a pass from a member whose Core does not stamp is accepted and its unstamped results dropped where stamps are compared, instead of the whole report being refused with 400; and the stamp now covers StorageClusterFence.credential_ref and PoolMember.fence_credential_version. docs/api/*.json and the generated reference are updated; generate_api.py --check passes and tests/test_api_contract.py passes.

roadmap.reason: The published roadmap describes shipped capability at a coarser grain than one fencing slice; the plan records that 4a is implemented and that 4b — the pool Corosync/Pacemaker cluster shared with clustered storage, sbd watchdog mode, arming, and the watchdog proof kind in promotion — remains.

state.reason: The watchdog capability is a host's own observation about its own hardware, recorded by the pool master in the membership record it owns. The Host fencing setting is a pool decision, so it is durable, replicated and only ever written by the master. Nex Controller relays the setting, displays the master's checklist and readiness, and keeps nothing of its own — only the command it journaled and its audit entry, which is how every other pool operation already works.
state.record: Durable, on the pool master, in pool-peer.json: PoolMembership.host_fencing_disabled (the pool's Host fencing setting, recorded as the negative so that a record written before the setting existed reads as on, which is the default) and PoolMember.watchdog (each host's own reported watchdog capability, written only when the finding changes so a settled pool does not re-sign and re-push its authority replica). Both ride the existing signed authority replica to every member, so a member holds the setting and every host's capability in its verified copy. NOT durable, deliberately: PoolMembership.fence_summary and PoolMember.fence_readiness, including the prerequisite checklist and the watchdog method, which the master computes over the membership it owns each time it reports and re-derives in full after a restart. A fresh Controller recovers all of it from inventory.managed.membership reported by the master, exactly as it recovers the fence devices and identities: it asks the master and shows what the master says, and a master that is not reporting reads as unknown rather than as off. There is no Controller table, cache or file for any of it.

verification.method: Go unit tests in internal/vmhost against a fake sysfs tree built per case, and in internal/agent against in-process two- and three-host pool labs over the real mutual-TLS peer transport; Controller tests against the real HTTP handlers and journal; React unit tests (node src/*.test.mjs) and npx tsc --noEmit; a real-browser review of the new states in a fixture page; python3 scripts/generate_api.py --check; python3 scripts/check_docs.py --worktree; python3 -m unittest discover -s tests. RESULTS, all run in this working tree on 2026-09-22: go build ./... PASS; go vet ./internal/... PASS; go test -count=1 ./internal/... PASS (all packages); go test -race -count=1 ./internal/agent/ ./internal/vmhost/ PASS; npx tsc --noEmit PASS; every web/src/*.test.mjs PASS; python3 scripts/generate_api.py --check PASS; python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' PASS; python3 scripts/check_docs.py --worktree PASS. DETECTION: TestWatchdogDetectionClassifiesByDriver covers a chipset TCO, an AMD SP5100, the management controller's own timer registering with no driver link, softdog, an unrecognised driver, a device something else already holds open, and no watchdog at all; TestWatchdogDetectionPrefersTheHardwareDevice covers a host with both. NEVER-OPENS PROOF: TestWatchdogDetectionNeverOpensTheDeviceNode asserts detection is complete from sysfs with no device node present anywhere, and that no string literal in internal/vmhost/watchdog.go names a path under /dev — opening /dev/watchdog is what arms it on most drivers, so this is the property that must not be able to rot. REPORTING: TestAHostsWatchdogReachesTheMastersMembership asserts the master records its own and the member's, that the membership generation does not move, that twenty further identical passes move neither the generation nor the authority digest, and that a changed capability is recorded on the next pass; TestAMemberCannotAdvertiseAnInvalidOrForeignWatchdog posts over a member's own authenticated peer client and asserts an unsupported kind is refused with 400 and recorded nowhere, and that a valid report is credited to the caller and never written onto another host's row. SETTING: TestHostFencingIsADurableReplicatedPoolSetting asserts the default is on, that a member refuses to record it, that the master records it durably, that re-sending the same state succeeds rather than conflicting, that a command carrying no host fencing request is refused, that a frozen authority (a master change in flight) refuses the change and writes nothing, that the setting reaches the member's verified replica, and that the master reports it back — which is exactly what a fresh Controller reads. READINESS: TestAWatchdogIsNeverReadinessYetAndSaysWhy asserts no host is ever ready through a watchdog in this slice, that the pool count is therefore unchanged, and that each reason says the right thing including the setting being off and a host too old to report; TestATwoHostPoolSaysAWatchdogDoesNotApply asserts not_applicable and that the wording contains no pending language; TestTheMasterReportsThePrerequisiteChecklist asserts the four lines, that unmet lines name the hosts, that quorum is honestly unknown, and that giving every host a hardware watchdog closes that line and nothing else. CONTROLLER: TestHostFencingIsRelayedAndTheChecklistIsMirrored asserts a master without the capability is offered no switch and refuses the request with 409, that the capability, the summary, the checklist and the host's watchdog report all reach the client verbatim, that the relayed command is valid and names the master, that an exact retry makes no second row, and that a request with no request_id is refused. SLICE 3 FINDINGS: TestAFenceCredentialIsParsedAndNeverExecuted round-trips ordinary, quoted and shell-metacharacter passwords and asserts that four byte sequences which WOULD yield a password through a shell — a command before the printf, a bare echo, an unterminated value and an empty file — are all refused; the stamp fix has a new sub-case in TestReplacingAFenceDeviceDropsTheChecksTakenAgainstTheOldOne that was VERIFIED TO FAIL with the credential fields removed from PoolFenceProfileStamp ('a rotated fence credential inherited the old password's check'); TestAnUnstampedFenceCheckIsAcceptedAndAMalformedOneIsNot covers the older-member degradation and that a malformed stamp is still refused. BROWSER REVIEW: the real pool-members and pool-promotion modules were bundled with the project's own esbuild into an untracked local scratch directory (never web/dist) and driven in headless Chromium through Playwright over five fixture reports — a five-host pool with a hardware watchdog nothing arms, a software-only host, an unrecognised driver, a host with none and a host too old to report; a two-host pool; a pool with the setting turned off; a master too old for the setting; and a master that is not reporting — plus the loading and error states PoolMembers renders itself. Captures were inspected: every row carries its watchdog line under the fence device, the badge is never changed by the watchdog (a host with a ready management controller still reads 'BMC · checked from 2 hosts' with the unarmed-watchdog line beneath it), the switch shows the state the master records rather than the state last sent, the consequence and the checklist are on the page without opening anything, the checkbox is operable from the keyboard alone and opens no dialog, and a master that is not reporting says the setting is unknown rather than off. No console error was raised. ONE DEFECT WAS FOUND AND FIXED, then re-captured: the checklist's state badges were of different widths so the four line names did not align, which is fixed with a fixed-width badge column.
untested: NO PHYSICAL WATCHDOG DEVICE OF ANY MODEL HAS BEEN READ. Detection is exercised against fake sysfs trees only. The plan's acceptance gate requires physical-hardware evidence naming the exact watchdog models tested; that is outstanding. In particular, which attributes a real driver exposes varies — the in_use reading depends on the kernel exposing 'state', which not every driver does, and a driver that exposes none of them is reported honestly as what little sysfs said.

NO WATCHDOG HAS BEEN ARMED AND NO HOST HAS BEEN RESET, by design: nothing in this slice arms anything. The acceptance gate's partitioned-minority test, the bound before a proof is valid, and the refusals with a software-only watchdog and without quorum all belong to slice 4b and are untested here.

The hardware-driver list is a judgement from the kernel's own driver names, not a survey of shipped hardware. A driver outside it is reported as unknown and counts as nothing, which is the safe direction, but a host with real hardware and an uncommon driver will read as unprotected by watchdog until the driver is added. Classification by identity string is only a fallback for drivers that register with no parent device.

The prerequisite checklist's quorum line is hard-coded to unknown with Core's own sentence, because this pool runs no quorum service. It is not wired to Corosync, and slice 4b must replace that one line rather than add a second source for it.

Whether the Host fencing setting should also govern 'opting into the restarted-master restriction' was checked against the platform plan and the existing code and deliberately NOT wired here: the restarted-master restriction (poolPeerState.Restricted and recordPoolSelfFenceExposure) is today driven by whether a host has ever been fence-exposed, is enforced by Core before any start path, and has no opt-in switch of its own. Making it follow this setting would change a safety refusal that exists independently of watchdogs, which is not this slice's scope. It is flagged for 4b, where arming actually happens.

The browser review used mocked API data in a fixture page, not a running Controller against real hosts. It proves the wording, the states, the keyboard behaviour and that the consequence is visible without opening anything; it does not prove the projection end to end, which the Go and Controller tests cover separately.

Controller replacement is proven at the level this slice owns — the setting is in the master's durable replicated membership and the master reports it back, which is what a fresh Controller reads. No whole Controller was rebuilt against a live lab pool.

The fence-credential parser refuses anything that is not the one format FencePasswordScript produces, and the format has exactly one producer. A credential recorded in some other shape by a future or foreign writer would be refused rather than opened; the virsh SSH-key credential is a different store entry and a different path and is untouched. No credential in the old shape exists to migrate: the BMC credential is uncommitted work of this same plan.
